figure_verdicts.render_check: 1400x721 render; outer 2 px frame carries zero non-white pixels; four identified ink colours and no fifth.

rubric.contrast: pass. Text is #0b0b0b on white (about 18:1) and tick labels #52514e (about 7.3:1). Linear blue #2e6fb7 computes to about 5.2:1 on white and constant #1a1a1a to about 17:1, so every data series clears the 3:1 floor. The 0.5 percent threshold is #929292 dotted, about 3.1:1, which is the reference grey role and is additionally distinguished by its dot pattern and its short legend swatch.
rubric.data_ink: pass. Marks are the only ink carrying information: 4544 px of linear blue, 2769 px of constant near-black, 930 px of the dotted grey 0.5 percent threshold, plus ticks and axis titles. There is no fill, no shading, no gradient and no marker size that would swamp a neighbour; the largest marker is 8 px square.
rubric.decoration: pass. White page only. No gridlines, no band, no drop shadow, no title box, no background tint; the top and right spines are off and the only furniture is the two scales and their labels.
rubric.label_collision: pass. Zero non-white pixels in the outer 2 px frame, so no text artist is clipped at the canvas edge. Axis tick labels on both log scales are spaced at least 31 px apart in the tightest y spacing (0.001 to 0.0005) against about 19 px of glyph height, and the closest data markers clear every label: the lowest marker clears the bottom axis by 17 px, the right-hand hollow square sits inside the frame, and the black circle nearest the dotted threshold sits just above it with visible separation.
rubric.legibility: pass. A log-log error-against-unknowns plot over one frameless three-column legend ('constant, uniform' black dashed circles, 'linear, dipole' blue dashed diamonds, 'linear, finite loop' blue solid diamonds, 'constant, graded' hollow squares, '0.5 % target' dotted grey). Every series is traceable at a glance: the three linear arms step down by decade across the width, and the top two dipole diamonds are one pixel apart vertically but about 90 px apart horizontally, so they read as two points rather than one. Axis labels 'magnetisation unknowns' and 'worst-probe shielding error [%]' are full and unclipped.
rubric.table_form: pass. The image carries a monotone. The content is a continuous cost-against-accuracy tradeoff across two decades of unknowns and four decades of error, with a threshold crossing; a table of the same numbers (and the reviewed evidence fragment does have one) cannot show where each family crosses 0.5 percent or how the linear arms separate from the reference floor. The figure is the right form for the relationship it reports.

item_verdicts.caption_independence: pass. The caption under the figure in docs/evidence/fragments/iron-core-magnetisation/icm-linear-assembly-cost.html does not repeat a title: the figure carries no title element at all, and the caption states the machine case (mu_r = 1000 closed shell), which lane assembled and which solved. It states the axis scales and that every major tick is labelled, names the 0.5 percent dotted threshold, describes what the two linear curves do (finite-loop continues down while the dipole approaches its reference floor), and says the SVG was rendered to PNG and inspected with the save check passing for 27 text artists. It is a description a reader can check against the picture, and the picture agrees with it.
